_notes: Every gameplay number used by the hazard, survival, crawler, combat, drone, party (task L), guide, waves and hold (task T) modules. Distances are world pixels (the camera is at zoom 2), speeds are px/s, *Ms is milliseconds, *Sec is seconds. Each section has its own _notes. The player walks at 90 px/s, which most speeds here are balanced against.

survival._notes: Hazard ticks on the player's feet. Toxicity changes smoothly every frame; health damage is dealt in ticks (hazardTickSec) so the red damage flash isn't constant. With 'healer' in the party, toxicity decays faster. At 100 toxicity health drains. Contact hits (crawlers) give i-frames with an alpha flicker.

hazards._notes: Ambient particles over hazard rectangles: subtle, because the map art already shows the pools, corruption and fires. Emission rate scales with the rect's area (one particle per areaPerParticle px² each second, capped). Emitters outside the camera view are paused. depth sits just above the map background (-1) and below every actor.

crawler._notes: Nanite crawlers. They wander inside their group radius, chase once the player is within aggroRadius, give up when the player is beyond loseInterestRadius (or they are leashRadius from home) and walk back home. chaseSpeed stays below the player's 90 so you can always run away.

combat._notes: SPACE strike (needs the has_weapon flag). The hitbox is hitboxLength deep in the facing direction and hitboxWidth across it. The lunge is a short velocity shove through player.pushBack, so walls still block it.

drone._notes: Warden drones never deal damage. The vision cone is coneRange px long and coneAngleDeg wide, gently sweeping ±sweepDeg around the travel direction. Colliders block line of sight (and clip the drawn cone). Seeing the player fills detection from 0 to 1 in detectionFillSec; otherwise it drains in detectionDrainSec. At 1 the drones call onCaught().

party._notes: Followers walk the player's recorded path. A point is recorded each time the player moves recordStepPx. Follower N aims for the point spacing × N px back along that path. Far behind (catchUpDistance) they walk faster.

guide._notes: The gold guide trail (world/Guide.js). The map is cut into cellPx cells; colliders are inflated by the player's 16x10 feet body (+ padPx clearance) and A* (8 directions, no corner cutting) finds a route that is then string-pulled into straight lines. A search runs every recomputeMs while the player moves, at once if the target changes or the player moves more than moveThresholdPx. Walkability is exact: a cell is walkable if the 16x10 body at its centre (or, for edge cells, at a spot on a 2 px sub-grid inside it) overlaps no collider. maxNodes caps one search (the route then stops at the closest cell found). A target inside a wall snaps to the nearest free spot within snapRadiusCells; if that spot can't be reached, any reachable spot within reachPx (interaction range) will do. No route: retry once with a 12x8 body; still none: no trail. Crumbs (an fx-glow halo at `scale` in `color`, plus a brighter core at coreScale in coreColor, both additive) sit every spacingPx from startPx to maxPx along the route: they fade in over nearFadePx, dim to farAlpha with distance and fade out over the last farFadePx. A brightness wave (waveLengthPx apart, moving waveSpeedPx/s toward the target) adds waveBoost alpha and waveScale size. The trail fades in/out at fadePerSec. depth sits just above the ground (-1) and below actors. Each crumb also has a soft dark shadow (shadowScale, shadowAlpha) under it, so the gold reads on bright grass as well as on dark ground.

waves._notes: The finale's crawler swarm (world/Waves.js). interval/perWave/maxAlive/aggro/tag are the defaults for waves.start(); the scene may override them. The first wave comes firstDelayMs after start(). A wave that would exceed maxAlive spawns only what fits; if nothing fits it waits retryMs. Vents outside the camera view (grown by offscreenPadPx) are preferred. Crawlers appear within ventJitterPx of the vent, fade in over spawnFadeMs and roam wanderRadius around it until the player is within aggro. Hunters that can't see the player follow a distance field on a cellPx grid (walls grown by padPx so they never snag on corners), rebuilt every fieldEveryMs, looking ahead lookaheadCells. All timers pause while input is locked.

hold._notes: Relay hold zones (world/HoldPoint.js). Standing inside fills progress over `duration` ms; outside it drains at decayFraction of the fill speed (0.25 = four times slower). Frozen while input is locked. 'hold' events go out at most every emitEveryMs (plus at once on every state change). The floor ring is an ellipse ringInsetPx inside the rect, pulsing every ringPulseMs at ringDepth (above the ground, below actors); completion flashes for flashMs. AEGIS field: while the player holds a relay it pulses every pulseEveryMs, hitting crawlers within pulseRadius px for pulseDamage (with knockback), so a knocked-back player can step back in. Progress only starts draining after graceMs outside.
